title: Rice Production — East Africa Upland and Lowland
content:
## Rice (Oryza sativa) — East Africa

Rice consumption is rising rapidly in East Africa. Production occurs in irrigated schemes (Mwea Kenya, Mbeya Tanzania, Ukerewe Tanzania) and rainfed upland systems.

### Recommended Varieties

**Irrigated lowland:**
- **Basmati 370 / Basmati 217** — aromatic, premium market (Kenya highlands)
- **IR 2793-80-1** — high yield irrigated
- **BW 196** — Tanzania irrigated schemes

**Upland / rainfed (NERICA):**
- **NERICA 4, NERICA 10** — drought-tolerant; Uganda, western Kenya, Tanzania
- **WAB 56-50** — early maturing upland

### Planting

- **Irrigated:** Transplant 21-day seedlings at 20cm × 20cm; maintain 5–10cm water depth
- **Upland:** Direct seed at onset of rains, 25cm row spacing
- **Seed rate:** 40–60 kg/ha (transplanted); 80–100 kg/ha (direct seeded)

### Fertilizer

- Basal DAP 100 kg/ha at planting/transplanting
- Topdress Urea 50 kg/ha at tillering (25–30 days)
- Second split 25 kg Urea/ha at panicle initiation if soil is poor

### Rice Blast (Magnaporthe oryzae)

**Symptoms:** Diamond-shaped lesions with grey centers and brown margins on leaves; neck rot on panicles causes empty grains ('white heads').

**Control:**
- Plant resistant varieties (check KALRO/ARI releases for local blast races)
- Avoid excessive nitrogen
- Tricyclazole (Beam) or Azoxystrobin at first sign; 2–3 sprays at 14-day intervals
- Seed treatment with fungicide before planting in blast-prone areas
content_sw:
## Mchele (Oryza sativa) Afrika Mashariki

Matumizi ya mchele yanazidi kuongezeka Afrika Mashariki.

### Aina

- **Basmati 370** — harufu nzuri, soko la juu Kenya
- **NERICA 4, NERICA 10** — vinastahimili ukame; Uganda na magharibi Kenya

### Rice Blast (Magnaporthe)

Dalili: vidonda vya almasi kwenye majani; shingo ya panicle inaoza ('white heads').

Tiba: panda aina zinazostahimili; epuka nitrojeni nyingi; dawa ya kuvu Tricyclazole au Azoxystrobin.

title: Sorghum — Drought-Tolerant Cereal for Drylands
content:
## Sorghum (Sorghum bicolor)

Sorghum is the most important dryland cereal in semi-arid East Africa — ideal where maize fails due to drought.

### Recommended Varieties

**Grain types:**
- **Gadam Hamam** — Kenya coast and eastern lowlands; 90–100 days
- **Serena / Seredo** — Tanzania; good grain quality
- **Macia** — ICRISAT release; dual-purpose grain + fodder
- **KARI Mtama 1** — Kenya drylands

**Dual-purpose (grain + fodder):**
- **Sugar Drip** — sweet stalk for fodder + grain

### Planting

- Plant at onset of rains; depth 3–5cm
- Spacing: 75cm × 15cm (≈89,000 plants/ha) for grain; wider for fodder
- Seed rate: 10–15 kg/ha
- Can ratoon (regrow from stubble) after harvest in good soil moisture

### Fertilizer

- DAP 50 kg/ha at planting in poor soils
- Sorghum is efficient with low fertility — do not over-fertilize with nitrogen (lodging risk)

### Drought Tolerance

- Survives 3–4 weeks without rain after establishment
- Better than maize on sandy soils and in ASAL counties (Turkana, Wajir, Mandera, Karamoja)

### Key Pests

Stem borer, shoot fly, birds at milky stage — bird scaring or early planting to avoid peak bird season.
content_sw:
## Mtama (Sorghum bicolor)

Mtama ni nafaka muhimu zaidi maeneo kame Afrika Mashariki — unafaa pale mahindi yameshindwa na ukame.

### Aina

- **Gadam Hamam** — pwani na mashariki Kenya
- **Macia** — nafaka na malisho
- **KARI Mtama 1** — maeneo kame Kenya

### Upanzi

- Panda mwanzo wa mvua; umbali sentimita 75 × 15
- Mbolea: DAP kilo 50/hekta tu kwenye udongo duni

### Ukame

- Unaweza kustahimili wiki 3–4 bila mvua baada ya kuanza kukua

title: Finger Millet (Eleusine coracana) — Nutrition and Dryland Crop
content:
## Finger Millet (Eleusine coracana) — 'Wimbi' / 'Kalimbi'

Finger millet is a highly nutritious traditional crop, especially important in western Kenya (Kisii, Kuria, Luhya communities), parts of Uganda, and Tanzania.

### Varieties

- **P224** — Kenya high yield
- **U-15, Gulu E** — Uganda releases
- **Okhale 1** — Tanzania

### Planting

- Broadcast or row plant at onset of long rains
- Seed rate: 10 kg/ha (finger millet seed is tiny — mix with sand for even broadcasting)
- First weeding critical at 2–3 weeks
- Maturity: 3–4 months

### Nutritional Value

- High calcium and iron — important for child nutrition
- Stores well (low pest damage in grain stores) — good for food security

### Striga Control

Striga (witchweed) is a major problem in millet/maize fields:
- Use Striga-resistant varieties where available
- Crop rotation with legumes
- Apply organic matter to improve soil fertility
content_sw:
## Wimbi (Eleusine coracana)

Wimbi ni zao la jadi lenye virutubisho vingi — muhimu magharibi Kenya (Kisii, Kuria).

### Upanzi

- Panda mwanzo wa mvua za masika
- Mbegu kilo 10/hekta — changanya na mchanga kusambaza vizuri

### Faida

- Kalsiamu na chuma nyingi; huhifadhiwa vizuri bila kuharibiwa na wadudu

title: Wheat — Kenya Highlands Production
content:
## Wheat (Triticum aestivum) — Kenya Highlands

Wheat is grown primarily in Kenya highlands: Narok, Timau, Nakuru, Uasin Gishu (lower altitudes), and Meru.

### Varieties (KALRO / Kenya Seed)

- **Robin** — widely planted; good yield
- **Kwale** — stem rust resistant
- **Eagle 10** — high altitude
- **Duma** — drought tolerant mid-altitude

### Planting

- Plant during long rains (March–April) or short rains where irrigation available
- Seed rate: 110–140 kg/ha
- Row spacing: 15–20cm between rows

### Fertilizer

- DAP 100 kg/ha at planting
- Topdress CAN 100 kg/ha at tillering (GS30)

### Diseases

- **Stem rust (Ug99 race group):** Use resistant varieties (Kwale); fungicide Propiconazole if needed
- **Septoria leaf blotch:** Crop rotation; Mancozeb spray at flag leaf emergence
content_sw:
## ngano (Triticum aestivum) Milima Kenya

Ngano hulimwa Narok, Timau, Nakuru, na Meru.

### Aina

- **Robin** — mavuno mazuri
- **Kwale** — inakabiliana na kutu ya shina

### Mbolea

- DAP kilo 100/hekta wakati wa kupanda
- CAN kilo 100/hekta wakati wa tillering
